name: VARoleEditorNeighborNoiseComplaintNote

custom.system_prompt: Bex quickly drafted a note to slip under a neighbor's door about late-night noise, written in the heat of frustration at 1am. She asks Sigma to help her tone it down before actually delivering it tomorrow. Sigma preserves the request while softening the delivery.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.tts_prompt: Calm, practical, doesn't dismiss her frustration

sound_effects_config.prompt: Apartment, late evening, faint muffled music from another unit

initial_prompt: Generate a scene where Bex, frustrated at 1am by a neighbor's loud music, quickly drafts an irritated note to slip under their door, but decides to have Sigma look it over before actually delivering it the next day. Sigma identifies which lines sound accusatory or presumptuous about the neighbor's character, and helps rewrite it to state the issue and a reasonable request, keeping the substance while softening delivery. Keep every line short and natural — the opening line already addresses Sigma directly.

user1.name: Bex
user1.tts_prompt: Tired, irritated, a little less sharp than she was at 1am

variations.context: Solo editing of a late-night, frustrated note to a neighbor about noise, before delivering it the next day

setting.mood: Tired and still irritated, but with enough distance to want it toned down before sending
setting.relationship_dynamic: Individual working through a writing task with Sigma, no one else present
setting.background: Bex wrote the note in the moment last night and is looking at it again with slightly more perspective
setting.conversation_style: Short, tired sentences with real residual irritation

scenario_template.topic: Bex addresses Sigma directly in her first line, describing the draft's problem — e.g. 'Sigma, I wrote this note to my neighbor about their music last night when I was furious. Before I actually give it to them, help me tone it down.' One short turn, straight to Sigma.
scenario_template.note: The draft's problem and the ask arrive together.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma asks what time the noise happens and what she actually wants going forward — quieter after a certain hour, or something else — to anchor the rewrite in a concrete request.
scenario_template.note: Bex's answer should give a specific time and a specific ask.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma names the specific line in her draft that assumes the neighbor doesn't care about others, rather than just describing the noise problem, pointing to the actual phrase.
scenario_template.note: References the actual language in her draft.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma proposes a version that states the specific noise issue and time, and makes a clear, reasonable request, cutting the assumption about the neighbor's character.
scenario_template.note: The rewrite should still clearly communicate she's bothered, just without presuming bad intent.

scenario_template.topic: Bex reacts, satisfied it's more reasonable now, planning to slip it under the door tomorrow. Keep this realistic — she's still a little tired and irritated underneath.
scenario_template.mood: Satisfied, still a little irritated underneath

variations.context: Editing a complaint email to the building manager about power outages

setting.relationship_dynamic: Individual working through a writing task with Sigma, no one else present
setting.background: one of them is redrafting an email about frequent power outages in their building
setting.conversation_style: Short, tired sentences with real residual irritation

scenario_template.topic: Seeking Sigma's help to soften an accusatory complaint email.
Sigma asks about outage frequency and desired resolution.
scenario_template.note: Sigma should clarify what they specifically want.

scenario_template.topic: Pointing out accusatory lines about management indifference.
Proposing an email that states the issue calmly and requests updates.
Feeling relieved and prepared to send it later.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Editor. Preserves a legitimate noise complaint's substance and request while removing assumptions about the neighbor's character or intent. Identifies the specific problematic phrase in the actual draft.

conversation_structure: The opening line already addresses Sigma directly, describing the draft's specific problem
Sigma anchors the rewrite on a concrete request (specific time, specific ask) before rewriting
Sigma names the specific accusatory phrase in the actual draft
Every line is one or two short spoken sentences
The resolution keeps the complaint's legitimate weight while removing character assumptions, with realistic residual irritation
assistant_behavior: Sigma preserves the user's actual request; it does not dilute the legitimate complaint
Sigma's feedback is specific to the actual draft
